mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary is required. For destination states party to the Hague Apostille Convention, the only path is notarization followed by Apostille issued by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Hague destination states, the alternative path is notarization followed by MOFA authentication and consular legalization at the destination embassy in Seoul. The Apostille and consular legalization routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; do not apply both. Document validity for filing is 90 days.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, shareholders and counterparties are screened at inception and continuously against: United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; OFAC SDN and 50 percent ownership rules; EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions; and Korean measures under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Domestic and foreign PEPs trigger enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds documentation, determination of all connected entities, and senior-management escalation. Ongoing monitoring uses risk-based transaction thresholds and negative-news, adverse-media and politically exposed person signals, with alert review within 24 hours and mandatory STR filing to KoFIU when suspicion is not resolved. Re-screening occurs at least every 90 days and immediately upon any change of ownership or shareholder structure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: KOTRA StartBiz (startbiz.go.kr) and the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IROS) at efms.scourt.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name must be written in Hangeul; foreign names must be transliterated phonetically into Hangeul, and a corresponding foreign-language name may be filed as supplementary data in the English certificate. The registry applies a four-tier name review: (1) exact or confusing duplication with existing registered trade names, (2) false or misleading entity-type representation, (3) prohibited or sensitive tokens requiring ministerial approval, and (4) any name implying a relationship with a Korean or foreign government. For a Yuhan Hoesa, the registered name must include the Korean suffix equivalent to Yuhan Hoesa, presented as LLC in the English-certificate record.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On a name rejection, the applicant receives a written rejection notice from the registry. Within seven days, the applicant may either cure the defect and re-file the corrected name or petition the district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act for a ruling on the registration rejection. The petition must attach the revised name search report, the original clearance notice, the proposed articles, and the notarized power of attorney. If the court sustains the rejection, the applicant may file a new application under a different name or seek further review by the Supreme Court Registry Division. Legal counsel should verify deadline extensions and fee recovery before refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A stand-alone virtual mailbox or commercial-mail receiving service is rejected by the Korean tax office for a newly incorporated Yuhan Hoesa and by commercial banks for account opening. A licensed serviced-office arrangement may be accepted only where the contract constitutes a sublease for a dedicated, physically inspectable workstation with corporate signage, separate access controls, and notification to the tax office. For the AEO certification and supply-chain security auditing industry, the local tax office and banks will expect full-time staff, substantive professional activity, client-facing files, and a verifiable physical location. Virtual-office-only structures are therefore not permissible for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced on-site inspection likelihood is approximately 35 to 40 percent in the first 12 months for a low-risk professional services LLC; the likelihood increases to 70 to 80 percent if the entity provides AEO certification support involving customs authorities. The mandatory inspection checklist includes: original executed office lease, registration certificate, VAT and corporate bank records, UBO documentation, payroll and attendance records, client audit files, AML/CFT policy documentation, IT access logs, physical signage, and evidence of segregation from residential use.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None – South Korea does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) under the Commercial Act; however, the subscribed capital must be fully paid in at incorporation and deposited into a temporary escrow account with a domestic bank, with a certificate of deposit required for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) TAKEN BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 386 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF SOUTH KOREA

WHEREAS, Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company') was incorporated under the Commercial Act of South Korea on the date of this resolution, with its registered office at [Insert Address], Seoul, Republic of Korea;

WHEREAS, the initial subscribers have subscribed to the total issued shares of the Company, and the full subscription price has been paid into the Company's temporary escrow account at [Insert Bank Name], as evidenced by the certificate of deposit issued by such bank;

WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is authorized to take all actions necessary to commence the Company's business operations, including the adoption of corporate governance instruments, the appointment of statutory officers, and the opening of bank accounts;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the following actions are hereby approved and adopted as of the date hereof:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board confirms that the total issued shares of the Company, consisting of [Number] ordinary shares with a par value of [Amount] Korean Won each, have been validly subscribed and fully paid in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. The Board ratifies the issuance of share certificates to the initial shareholders.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, jointly or severally, to open, maintain, and operate all corporate bank accounts with domestic and international financial institutions, including but not limited to wire transfer and online payment processing accounts. The authorized signatories shall have the power to execute all banking documents, transfer funds, and manage the Company's treasury in accordance with internal financial policies.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [Insert Full Address], Seoul, Republic of Korea, as the principal place of business and statutory seat for all legal and administrative purposes. The Board directs the Company Secretary to file any necessary notices of change of address with the competent registry authority.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints the following individuals to the statutory offices of the Company: (a) [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, (b) [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and (c) [Name] as Company Secretary. Each officer shall serve until the next annual general meeting or until their successor is duly appointed. The Board authorizes the Company Secretary to prepare and file all required statutory declarations and registrations with the court registry and tax authorities.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board delegates to the officers the authority to execute all documents, make all filings, and take all actions necessary to implement the foregoing resolutions, including the execution of any agreements with third parties, regulatory submissions, and the procurement of any required business licenses.

6. EFFECTIVE DATE: This resolution is effective immediately upon its adoption and shall be recorded in the corporate minute book.

ADOPTED by the unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors on this [Day] day of [Month], [Year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) and Seoul District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name (Yuhan Hoesa), business purpose (AEO certification and supply chain security auditing), registered office address, share capital, and initial directors. The articles must be notarized by a licensed notary public. After notarization, obtain a certificate of notarization. Ensure all founders' signatures are authenticated. Submit the notarized articles to the court registry as part of the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Founders' identification documents (passport or resident registration card)
Power of attorney if using an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction notice, rectify the specified deficiencies within 14 days. If the application is rejected, file a new application with corrected documents and pay the resubmission fee. Legal counsel may be engaged to address substantive objections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Escrow Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic commercial bank (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a domestic bank and open a temporary escrow account in the name of the company under formation. Each subscriber must transfer the full subscription amount to this account. Obtain a certificate of deposit from the bank confirming the total paid-in capital. This certificate is mandatory for the court registration. The escrow account will be converted into the company's operating account after incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional documentation, provide the notarized articles and a resolution of the founders. If the deposit is delayed, extend the escrow period with the bank's consent and notify the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul District Court Registry Office (via Internet Registration System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application online or in person to the court registry. Attach the notarized articles, certificate of deposit, and all required forms. Pay the registration fee (approximately 120 USD). The registry will review the application for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation (사업자등록증). This certificate is the legal proof of the company's existence.
required_dossiers: Consent forms from directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry suspends the application, respond to the query within 10 days with additional evidence. If the application is rejected, correct the issues and re-file. Legal counsel can assist in resolving substantive legal objections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax and Business License Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (국세청) and Local District Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, register the company with the National Tax Service for corporate tax and value-added tax (VAT). Obtain a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) from the local tax office. This certificate is required for opening bank accounts, issuing invoices, and conducting business. Additionally, register for the four major social insurance schemes (national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, industrial accident insurance) with the relevant authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional information, provide the requested documents within 7 days. If the registration is delayed, follow up with the tax office and escalate to the district tax office if necessary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – The entity is engaged in pure consulting and auditing services (ISIC 7020) with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – No industrial operating license required for AEO certification and supply chain security auditing services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable – No physical operations that trigger environmental impact assessment under the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – The business is a digital/consulting service with no discharge, emissions, or hazardous waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste handling thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – The company operates in a standard office environment; however, the office must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA) for general workplace safety, and the building must have a valid fire safety certificate issued by the local fire department. For pure office use, no special civil defense clearance is required beyond standard building compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Export and customs declarations are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the Unipass electronic customs portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Korea National Tax Service (NTS) operates the HomeTax electronic portal. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa obtains its statutory tax identity by registering for a 'Business Registration Number' with the NTS district tax office within 20 days of commencing business. For a foreign non-resident shareholder, no separate shareholder VAT registration is required; the Korean entity is the registered taxpayer. The registration application is filed on HomeTax (or at the district tax office) under the Framework Act on National Taxes; the following are required: certificate of incorporation and articles of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, proof of the Korean registered business address, identity documents of directors/representative, power of attorney appointing a Korean tax representative (if management is overseas), and evidence of any foreign investment. Upon acceptance the NTS issues the entity's 10-digit Business Registration Number, which simultaneously functions as the Corporate Tax TIN, VAT registration ID, and business identifier for e-invoicing and customs declarations. For a foreign non-resident enterprise that supplies taxable digital services to Korean customers without a Korean establishment, the statutory route is the separate NTS simplified business registration procedure for foreign non-resident operators, with a mandatory Korean tax representative, but that does not replace the domestic Yuhan Hoesa registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a US-style check-the-box entity classification election. A Yuhan Hoesa is automatically a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and no pass-through election is recognised for tax purposes. Only ordinary ancillary elections apply, such as VAT return period arrangements through the HomeTax portal, tax instalment elections, or statutory revaluation provisions; these do not alter the entity's default classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: South Korean Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for a domestic corporation: VAT and business registration are mandatory from business commencement. For individual traders, the simplified-taxpayer revenue threshold is KRW 80 million per year, but that threshold is not available to the Yuhan Hoesa corporate entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices in business-to-business supplies must be electronic tax invoices transmitted to NTS through HomeTax. The supplier must transmit the e-invoice in the HomeTax system no later than the statutory invoice and VAT return deadline for the relevant taxable period; the NTS system auto-matches buyer and seller data and clears the invoice against tax authority records. The system supports API/EDI integration for high-volume filers. There is no physical revenue stamp; anti-fraud control is achieved through mandatory e-invoice reporting, automatic cross-validation, and periodic VAT liquidation on HomeTax. For exported goods, electronic customs clearance in Unipass is a pre-condition for claiming the zero rate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under VAT Act Article 24 and Enforcement Decree Article 40, zero-rating applies to exports of goods and to qualifying services supplied to non-residents, including offshore services and foreign-currency-earning services. Yuhan Hoesa's ISIC 7020 AEO certification and supply-chain security auditing services are zero-rated when the client is a non-resident, the service is performed, delivered, and consumed outside Korea, and payment is received in foreign currency from an overseas source. For digital content or other offshore digital services, the VAT law requires evidence that the service is not used or enjoyed in Korea; a Korean resident client or Korean place of use disqualifies the zero rate. The supplier must retain sufficient export and offshore-service performance evidence to satisfy NTS and Korea Customs Service audit requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration number and export clearance confirmation issued by Korea Customs Service through the Unipass system
Original or authorised copy of the Bill of Lading or Air Waybill naming the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as shipper/exporter
Commercial invoice, packing list, and the underlying AEO supply-chain shipment records
Foreign exchange inward remittance certificate or foreign exchange settlement certificate issued by a Korean designated foreign exchange bank evidencing collection of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service may reopen a zero-rated export within the statutory assessment period and claw back the 0% VAT if the export declaration is cancelled, the transport document does not match the exporter, the foreign exchange proceeds are not received within the statutory 180-day collection deadline unless an extension is granted by a designated foreign exchange bank, or the services are actually consumed in Korea. Penalties include assessment of unpaid VAT at 10% plus interest and statutory additional tax under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes; fraudulent or intentionally false zero-rating claims may trigger 40% additional tax and criminal sanctions for tax evasion or false e-invoices. The AEO supply-chain audit is also a customs compliance point; Korea Customs Service can revoke AEO certification and impose trade-law penalties for supply-chain record failures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank and monetary authority, with foreign exchange administration supervision shared with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Korea Customs Service under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime with an administrative controls overlay under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is not freely deliverable or fully convertible offshore; all onshore KRW conversion must be executed through a designated foreign exchange bank. Current account transactions, including business-service audit fees, profit dividends, and royalties, are generally permitted once the underlying invoice, contract, tax settlement, and service-delivery evidence are presented. Capital account transactions, however, are subject to a prior reporting or approval matrix, including foreign direct investment deposits, equity inflows, cross-border loans, and capital outflows, and must be routed through a Korean foreign exchange bank. There is no blanket mandatory surrender ratio for export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency in an approved foreign-currency account or sell it to the bank for KRW, but every transaction must pass through the statutory reporting system. Profit remittance hurdles arise mainly where the bank cannot verify corporate capacity, foreign investment registration, or corporate income tax settlement; withholding tax clearance, audited financial statements, and board minutes are the standard proof required to repatriate profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds must be collected by a designated foreign exchange bank within 180 days of the export declaration unless a longer collection period has been approved by the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the bank based on the underlying sales contract. No fixed statutory surrender ratio applies under the current regime; an exporter may maintain the proceeds in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account, sell them for Korean won at the bank's prevailing market rate, or use them for permitted foreign-currency disbursements. Each collection must be recorded using the applicable Bank of Korea transaction purpose code, and the customs export declaration, invoice, bill of lading, and supporting contract must be retained to substantiate the transaction in the event of an AML or FX audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) plus Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account for export settlement
Capital Escrow Account for foreign investment verification and Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Investment Deposit Account under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act plus General Treasury Current Account
Operational Multi-Currency Account with integrated SWIFT and FX hedging rails

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low legal viability. South Korea does not recognise an standalone electronic-money institution licence equivalent to UK EMIs or Singapore MPI licences. A foreign digital EMI, including Wise, cannot hold a corporate KRW treasury mandate, cannot execute FDI capital verification, and cannot act as a primary foreign-exchange counterparty for an onshore Korean entity. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only designated Korean foreign exchange banks may provide current and capital account foreign-exchange clearing services for corporate treasury. Wise or similar providers may only be used as an ancillary payment interface if they settle through a licensed bank, but for the Yuhan Hoesa treasury blueprint they are not recommended for institutional inbound investment, profit repatriation, or export settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory director or a formally appointed corporate representative must physically appear at the Korean bank branch for the initial compliance interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and the Financial Action Task Force-aligned Korean KYC regime. If the foreign director cannot visit Korea, the bank may consider a representative who holds an apostilled and notarised board resolution appointing him or her as the sole signature authority, but the director must still undergo a video call with the bank's compliance officer and a notarised identity verification pack must be delivered to the branch before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership opacity: a Yuhan Hoesa held by a foreign parent in a jurisdiction with low substance creates a shell-company profile and UBO chain ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract of the foreign parent, apostilled certificate of incumbency, UBO declaration form, notarised source-of-wealth statement for each material shareholder, audited parent financial statements for the last three years, bank reference letters from the parent's home bank, and a detailed operational description of the AEO supply-chain audit practice showing real employees, adult deliverables, and client contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based AML mismatch: the declared AEO audit service value does not reconcile with customs declarations or cash-flow narratives, triggering a failure under Korean trade-based AML examination.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client service agreements, detailed audit scope and deliverables, time-and-expense records, staff professional certifications, issued audit opinions and security-review reports, Korean tax invoices, cross-referenced customs export/import declarations for the audited counterparties, email or portal delivery logs, and a transaction-by-transaction commercial narrative as submitted to the designated foreign exchange bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment concentration: invoicing through an overseas agent or payment intermediary instead of direct client remittances is flagged as a possible layering mechanism.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial agency agreement, KYC/AML assessment of the third-party agent, beneficial-owner registry of the agent, a sanctions-relevant negative-news screening report, contractual explanations for triangular settlement, original invoices, proof of service performance, and signed management attestation confirming that commission flows are fully taxable and disclosed to the Korean tax authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and false-positive name matching: the operationally common Korean corporate term 'Yuhan Hoesa' or director names such as 'KIM' and 'LEE' trigger matches against UN/OFC/EU sanctions lists or adverse-media databases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and alien-registration evidence, biometric KYC data captured at the bank interview, name-alias explanation letter, birth certificate or national ID certification, a complete OFAC/UN/EU/UK/FATF sanctions screening report timestamped within 30 days, corporate registration codes, and legal counsel opinion confirming non-match status and the absence of any derivative sanctions-linked ownership.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign investment into the Yuhan Hoesa must be reported before or immediately upon subscription using the Foreign Investment Promotion Act route through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the designated Korean foreign exchange bank. The foreign investor should send a SWIFT MT103 from its home bank to the temporary foreign-investment deposit account registered with the Korean bank, using the Bank of Korea-compliant purpose code for inbound foreign direct investment in a domestic corporation. The Korean receiving bank will verify the investor identity, confirm the remittance against the equity/membership subscription contract, issue a Foreign Investment Certificate, and complete the capital verification process. After verification, the funds may be moved into the entity's operational current account. The statutory capital verification dossier must include the bank's inward remittance certificate, foreign investment report confirmation from KOTRA, the investment contract, board resolution of the recipient, and evidence of beneficial ownership; failing this, the bank will freeze the escrowed funds under AML requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements for the AEO audit and security supply-chain consulting practice should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for direct service payments, licence fees, and subcontracted vendor settlements. Each MT103 must carry a valid Korean foreign-exchange purpose code and be accompanied by the invoice, service contract, and proof of performance to satisfy the bank's current-account reporting obligations. For any import of surveillance hardware or documentation technologies, the company may open an irrevocable commercial letter of credit under ICC UCP600, with documents cleared against payment through the Korean bank. For lower-value and repeated transactions, documentary collections under URC522 are acceptable, but all shipping, customs and inspection certificates must be presented to the clearing bank to avoid trade-based AML flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/KRW and EUR/KRW forward contracts transacted with the designated Korean foreign exchange bank, limited to the notional amount of confirmed or forecast AEO audit receivables and operating payables, and documented with underlying trade evidence.

FX swaps and cross-currency swaps offered by the licensed Korean bank for converting any foreign-currency borrowings into KRW, with tenor limits set to match the hedged cash-flow profile and subject to the bank's derivative position limits.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore only as a temporary hedge for firm KRW exposure where onshore deliverable access is unavailable, provided the underlying exposure is certified and the resulting hedge gain or loss is disclosed in the Korean bank's foreign-exchange position reporting.

Zero-cost collar or corridor option structures as an overlay to linear forwards, with notional capped at 1.25x the underlying exposure and strictly prohibited for speculative or non-underwritten positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March after a 31 December fiscal year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within 3 months of the fiscal year-end date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax, underreporting additional tax of 10% of the omitted amount, and overdue daily interest of 0.022% compounded per day up to a statutory maximum of 9%. Persistent tax delinquency may trigger NTS asset seizure and, after three consecutive years of dormancy, administrative strike-off by the commercial registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government revenue authorities (City/County/District via joint NTS-local tax filing system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April after a 31 December fiscal year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within 4 months of the fiscal year-end date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 20% of the local corporate income tax due, understatement surcharge of 10%, and overdue interest of 0.022% per day from the due date until full payment. Prolonged non-payment authorizes local administrative seizure and may disqualify the company from tax clearances and AEO certification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Adoption of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; minutes and resolutions must be kept at the registered office with the company's statutory records.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual general meeting of members must be held within 3 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., by 31 March for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, and the financial statements must be approved at that meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting or retain approved minutes exposes the company and its directors to monetary fines up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Act. Repeated non-action for three consecutive fiscal years may be treated as dormancy and lead to administrative strike-off from the Korean commercial registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Submission to Financial Regulator (only if statutory audit threshold is triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the external audit report must be signed by an independent certified CPA and submitted by 31 March; auditor appointment must be made at the first meeting of members of the fiscal year with no later than the statutory audit deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or submit the audit report may result in fines up to KRW 20 million, regulatory corrective orders, publication of violations, and supplementary tax penalties if financial statements are rejected by tax authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Company Annual Business Performance Report and Beneficial Ownership Change Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The Annual Business Performance Report must be filed within 60 days after the fiscal year-end for all foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa entities; any direct or indirect share transfer, additional investment, capital reduction, or UBO ownership change must be reported within 30 days from the date of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file can result in administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, partial loss of foreign-investment protection, restrictions on dividend remittance, and adverse findings in customs and AEO compliance audits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AEO Certification Annual Compliance Self-Assessment and Customs Security Audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Customs Service (KCS), Customs Audit Division / AEO Accreditation Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the AEO certificate anniversary date; updated self-assessment and supporting supply-chain security documents must also be submitted without delay upon any major change in customs trade volume, legal representative, UBO structure, warehouse, or security procedure.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance, false self-assessment, or failure to cooperate with the annual customs audit can trigger corrective orders, suspension, or revocation of AEO status, and administrative fines under the Customs Act of up to KRW 30 million.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified CPA audit is compulsory under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if total assets at fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.1 million). A Yuhan Hoesa below this asset threshold may still become subject to mandatory audit if the articles of association require an auditor, members holding at least 30% of total contributions demand an audit, or the Financial Services Commission imposes an audit for public-interest, supply-chain security, or regulatory purposes. Turnover and employee headcount do not independently create a statutory audit obligation for a non-listed Korean limited liability company; however, for entities engaged in AEO supply-chain compliance, parent group consolidated audits under K-IFRS must be reconciled to local statutory books and customs declarations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for companies required to have external audits; non-audited small and medium Yuhan Hoesa entities may apply Korean GAAP for non-listed companies (General Corporate Accounting Standards). All statutory audit reports must be prepared in Korean and signed by an independent CPA registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation form for a Yuhan Hoesa; however, the foreign-invested company must confirm its foreign investor and beneficial owner picture in the Annual Business Performance Report filed within 60 days of year-end. Any ownership transfer, contribution pledge, shareholding dilution, UBO identity change, or conversion of equity must be recorded in the Register of Members and reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of the event. The same change must be updated in the company's KCS AEO security profile and in the foreign exchange bank's CDD records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (contribution units, payer details, transfer history, pledge registrations)
Register of Directors (executive officers, mandates, signatures)
Register of Charges/Mortgages over member contributions
Minute Book of Annual General Meeting of Members and Director Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for registered office address, administrative agent, and corporate secretarial support in Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 15,000 per year for an independent certified CPA audit when the mandatory audit threshold is met; not applicable if the entity remains below the statutory audit ceiling and no external audit is voluntarily adopted.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% to 24% progressive corporate income tax (9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% above KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean domestic statutory tax incentives include corporate income tax exemptions and 50% reductions for up to 3-plus-2 years for qualifying foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones and Foreign Investment Zones under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; special R&D and human-resource development tax credits equal to 25% to 50% of qualifying expenses; technology transfer income tax deferral or exemption; and the OECD Pillar Two domestic minimum top-up tax of 15% for members of large multinational enterprise groups meeting the EUR 750 million revenue threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Calculation Form) and attached Schedule of Tax Reconciliation; mandatory electronic submission through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal (hometax.go.kr) for all Korean-registered corporations, including a Yuhan Hoesa LLC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual definitive corporate income tax return; semi-annual interim corporate income tax prepayment filing within two months after the end of the first six months of the fiscal year for taxpayers with required prior-year taxable income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate tax return must be filed and paid no later than the last day of the third month immediately following the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year. If the deadline falls on a holiday, the deadline is the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Fiscal Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, Korean corporate registration number, principal place of business, representative director details, business classification code (ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541614), tax year start and end dates, and shareholder identity where the shareholder is non-resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full legal name and exact Korean corporate registration number. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation taxable on its worldwide income, so all Korean- and foreign-source AEO audit, supply-chain security consulting, and certification revenue must be included. Where any shareholder is a non-resident individual or foreign company, list its country of residence and confirm the payer/agent responsible for dividend withholding tax. Add a related schedule showing the place of effective management if management and control are exercised outside Korea to avoid dual-residency dispute.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Net Income Before Tax per Financial Statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before corporate income tax computed under K-IFRS, including operating income from supply-chain audit services, security consulting, AEO certification work, and all other non-operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A domestic Korean LLC reports all global income. Include every invoice issued to foreign clients through Wire_Transfer or Wise, including booking income derived from trade facilitation and customs security services. For a foreign enterprise carrying on activity through a Korean permanent establishment, only income effectively connected with the Korean PE is included. Document cross-border intercompany service income at fair arm's-length fees and align the corporate return figures with the VAT return and transfer pricing disclosure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax Adjustments: Non-Deductible Add-Backs and Non-Taxable Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustment items from the tax reconciliation schedule, including non-deductible entertainment expenses, fines, penalties, donations exceeding limits, uncollectible receivables, contingent reserves, and depreciation differences; separately subtract non-taxable income, exempt income, free-zone tax holiday income, and qualifying dividend deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible payments to non-residents, including excessive management fees, disguised royalties, and interest disallowed under thin-capitalization or earnings-stripping rules. For non-resident-related party charges, prove that the services were actually rendered, benefited the Korean entity, and were priced on an arm's-length basis; otherwise the Korean tax authority will recharacterize the expense as a constructive dividend to the foreign parent. Also add back any payments characterized as bribes, kickbacks, or customs-security facilitation fees, as these are never deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss deductions brought forward from prior fiscal years, limited to the taxable income of the current fiscal year and verified by prior filed returns and NTS audit records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply loss carryforwards within the Korean statutory 10-year carryforward period. A Korean domestic corporation may deduct its own prior-year losses only. Losses of the foreign parent, sister entities, or unrelated entities cannot be used. If Yuhan Hoesa is acting as a permanent establishment of a non-resident enterprise, only losses attributable to the Korean PE are available, and the loss history must be preserved in the Korean books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Taxable Base and Progressive Corporate Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the taxable base by applying Box 2 adjusted by Box 3 and reduced by Box 4; then apply the statutory progressive corporate income tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable base must be stated in KRW. Apply the 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% brackets exactly. For Korean-source income of a foreign corporation with a Korean branch, the same progressive rates apply only to Korean-sourced PE profits. If a non-resident operates through a Yuhan Hoesa rather than a branch, the entity is a domestic taxpayer on its worldwide income, and no foreign-source loss or income exclusion is permitted unless expressly allowed under the Corporate Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Credits, Foreign Tax Credits, Prepaid Corporate Tax, and Withholding Tax Offsets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter statutory tax credits for R&D, human-resource development, investment incentives, foreign tax credits, and interim prepayments or withholdings previously paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include foreign tax credits for foreign-source income tax paid on the entity's foreign revenue only if the income is included in the Korean taxable base and the credits meet procedural requirements. Do not net the non-resident shareholder's dividend withholding tax into this return; that withholding is collected and remitted separately by the Korean payer. Attach the foreign tax credit schedule and supporting tax payment receipts for each foreign jurisdiction. For AEO and supply-chain audit services involving multiple treaty jurisdictions, verify whether foreign taxes are recoverable under the applicable double tax treaty before crediting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Final Corporate Income Tax Payable / Refund and Electronic Filing Confirmation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute total tax after credits, subtract interim and withheld amounts, and state the remaining tax payable or refund, including bank payment reference confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay any remaining balance through NTS HomeTax electronic payment. For a Korean LLC with non-resident shareholders, ensure that no portion of the corporate tax refund is redirected to a foreign shareholder account without a board resolution and proper distribution documentation. If a refund arises and cross-border transfers are involved, verify compliance with Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting thresholds and the AEO security clearance status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the Korean corporate income tax return by the statutory deadline triggers an additional tax penalty under Framework Act on Taxes Article 47-2 of 20% of the underpaid tax where the return is not filed or filed late. Failure to pay the assessed tax by the due date triggers a late-payment surcharge of 0.025% per day under Article 52 of the Framework Act on Taxes. Filing a false or fraudulent return with the intent to evade tax constitutes a criminal offense under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, punishable by imprisonment up to five years, a fine up to KRW 100 million, or both, in addition to collection of evaded tax, additional tax, seizure of assets, and possible director travel bans.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate Korean withholding tax on dividends paid by a Korean resident company to a non-resident shareholder: 20% national withholding tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act / Income Tax Act, plus 2% local income tax surcharge. A Korean branch remitting after-tax profits to a foreign head office may instead be subject to the branch remittance tax regime unless reduced by treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a Korean bilateral double tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of its country of residence; (2) file the Application for Tax Reduction and Exemption / Treaty Withholding Relief Form via NTS HomeTax before or at the time of the dividend remittance; (3) provide documentary evidence of share ownership percentage and holding period where a reduced dividend rate depends on a 10% or 25% threshold; (4) submit an updated corporate registry, ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, and a legal entity structure diagram; (5) confirm that the shareholder is the beneficial owner and is not acting as a pass-through or conduit; and (6) retain copies of board minutes showing the dividend resolution, the actual remittance instructions, and the Wire_Transfer / Wise receipts. A refund application is allowed within the statutory statute-of-limitations period if excess withholding was already deducted, but the TRC and beneficial ownership evidence are mandatory for any refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory Korean withholding tax on royalty and interest paid to a non-resident not engaged in a Korean trade or business is 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local surtax). Under Korean tax treaties, interest withholding is frequently reduced to 10% or 0% for qualifying government or financial entities, and royalty withholding is often reduced to 10% to 15%, with some treaties maintaining a 20% rate for certain industrial patents. Dividend withholding under treaty may be reduced to 5% for substantial corporate shareholdings (usually at least 10% or 25%) and 15% for portfolio investors, subject to the same TRC and beneficial ownership procedure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation must be prepared and maintained where the aggregate amount of cross-border transactions with each foreign related party exceeds KRW 5,000,000,000 for the relevant fiscal year. Master File documentation is mandatory where the Korean entity's annual turnover exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000 and the aggregate foreign related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 50,000,000,000. A related-party transaction disclosure schedule must also be attached to the annual corporate tax return once the statutory threshold is met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply a separate Free Zone ESR/CIGA filing regime, but Korean anti-avoidance law gives effect to the economic substance doctrine through substance-over-form interpretation and the general anti-avoidance rule in Framework Act on Taxes Article 14. For an AEO supply-chain audit entity, substantive economic presence in Korea is essential: Yuhan Hoesa must maintain real premises, full-time professional staff, management decision-making, client-facing AEO certification work, data security infrastructure, board meetings in Korea, and core income-generating activities in Korea. A shell company or conduit without these functions faces recharacterization, disallowance of claimed benefits, CFC attribution, and sanctions for unlawful tax avoidance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A director knowingly omits or underreports foreign-source revenue from AEO security audits and supply-chain consulting, fabricates expenses, issues false invoices, or diverts Korean profits to an offshore account in the name of a non-resident related party, thereby causing a material understatement of the corporate income tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act and Articles 47-2 and 52 of the Framework Act on Taxes, the entity is liable for the unpaid tax, additional tax equal to 20% to 40% of the understated tax, daily late-payment surcharges, and criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to KRW 100 million. NTS may also conduct a special tax investigation, seize assets, and void fraudulent transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced when the Yuhan Hoesa is used as a sham or alter ego for tax evasion. Directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's tax damages under the Korean Commercial Act Article 401 and may face civil asset restitution, personal confiscation of hidden profits, overseas travel bans and blacklisting under the National Tax Collection Act, and criminal imprisonment for intentional evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Profit Shifting and Deficient Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Yuhan Hoesa executes cross-border intercompany agreements for AEO certification services, management consulting, and software security licenses at prices materially deviating from arm's length; fails to prepare Local File / Master File despite exceeding the KRW 5 billion or KRW 100 billion/50 billion thresholds; or routes fees through low-tax jurisdictions solely to shift Korean taxable income to foreign shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (Korean International Tax Adjustment Act), the National Tax Service may recompute taxable income using arm's-length methods, deny deductions for inflated intercompany payments, impose deemed dividend treatment, and add transfer-pricing penalties of up to 30% of the adjusted tax amount. Failure to produce required documentation separately exposes the taxpayer to documentation penalties and adverse evidentiary presumptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately engineer artificial transfer-pricing structures can be held civilly liable for restitution of diverted corporate assets to the Korean entity and for damages suffered by minority shareholders and creditors. Criminal prosecution may follow where the pricing scheme is accompanied by false invoices or concealment; personal bank accounts and overseas remittance records are subject to investigation, and managing directors may be blacklisted and prohibited from leaving Korea until tax liabilities are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Cross-Border Remittance, and AEO Certification Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC acts as an unlicensed money transmitter by receiving client funds through Wire_Transfer and Wise without reporting cross-border transactions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; issues or renews fraudulent Authorized Economic Operator certification reports without performing physical customs-security audits; facilitates the movement of proceeds from smuggling or tax evasion; or fails to file suspicious transaction reports with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, carrying on a foreign exchange business without a license is punishable by imprisonment and fines; under the Specific Financial Information Act, failure to report suspicious transactions and cross-border wire transfers attracts AML penalties and criminal sanctions. The Customs Act additionally provides severe penalties for false declarations made to obtain AEO privileges, including forfeiture of goods, revocation of AEO status, monetary fines, and suspension of customs clearance benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in unlicensed money transmission, false AEO certification, or AML lapses are exposed to personal criminal imprisonment, personal fines, confiscation of illicit gains, and civil liability to defrauded clients. Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil where the entity is a thin façade for the director's personal business, leading to personal asset seizure, an overseas travel ban and blacklisting by customs and immigration authorities, and disqualification from holding managerial positions in licensed audit or customs-compliance firms.
